original_question: Which specific MSR heat-transport decisions require the outputs we propose: cooling duty, heat losses, circulation, extrema, freezing margin, response/settling or startup/shutdown predictions? Connect each output to a decision, mechanism and primary source.
review_answer: Duty/losses support heat-path and cooler sizing; circulation supports resistance and heat-transport comparisons; wall/fluid temperature distributions support material and freezing-margin reasoning; response and settling support operating-change planning. Tie each prediction to its control volume and use. Brown et al. supply liquid-fuel MSR phenomena, while circuit-specific passive-removal studies support particular heat paths. The review does not assign a universal reactor tolerance or turn facility sensor extrema into global safety margins.
evidence: S13 §V/Table II; S47 conclusions; S50/S51/S52; B§4
research_followup: Use the supported motivation and source/solid/fluid distinctions in the proposal; quantitative transfer is a later named-circuit assessment.
topic: Engineering decisions served by each output
integrated_takeaway: Duty/losses support heat-path and cooler sizing; circulation supports resistance and heat-transport comparisons; wall/fluid temperature distributions support material and freezing-margin reasoning; response and settling support operating-change planning.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Add a decision--output--mechanism table for duty, losses, circulation, temperature extrema and response; state which are measured or model-inferred.

original_question: How do requirements differ for liquid-fueled reactors, salt-cooled solid-fuel systems, primary/secondary loops and test facilities? Avoid one generic MSR justification.
review_answer: Liquid-fuel primary systems have moving-fluid heat generation and possible nuclear feedback; solid-fuel salt-cooled systems receive heat through fuel/structures; secondary circuits receive it through exchangers. Drain or passive-removal paths have different sources, boundaries and missions. The same loop may illuminate selected thermal mechanisms across these settings, but its validation and exclusions remain circuit-specific. For this study, motivate those needs broadly and claim facility thermal reduction/assessment first; nuclear kinetics, chemistry and irradiation are excluded.
research_followup: Use the supported motivation and source/solid/fluid distinctions in the proposal; quantitative transfer is a later named-circuit assessment.
topic: Which salt system or circuit is represented?
integrated_takeaway: Liquid-fuel primary systems have moving-fluid heat generation and possible nuclear feedback; solid-fuel salt-cooled systems receive heat through fuel/structures; secondary circuits receive it through exchangers.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Separate liquid-fuel primary, salt-cooled solid-fuel, secondary/passive circuit and test-facility purposes before making an MSR relevance claim.

original_question: What can natural-circulation/surrogate-fluid loops establish, and what requires property, geometric, source-distribution and dimensionless similarity? Compare Re, Pr, buoyancy measures, development lengths and conjugate thermal time scales where relevant. Explain which cannot all be matched simultaneously.
review_answer: Match the target mechanism through geometry, elevation and source/sink distribution as well as Re, Pr, a declared buoyancy measure, hydraulic/thermal development and fluid/solid response ratios. Simultaneous matching can be incompatible with real surrogate properties and wall materials. Report unavoidable distortions and their target sensitivity. High Pr or identical correlation-evaluated Nu is insufficient for quantitative circuit equivalence. Facility prediction and mechanism analogy remain useful results even when full circuit similarity cannot be achieved.
evidence: S56 Eqs1–16; S64 Eqs2–10/Table V; S74 §4.1/Table4.10; B§6
research_followup: Use the supported motivation and source/solid/fluid distinctions in the proposal; quantitative transfer is a later named-circuit assessment.

proposed_work_or_expansion: Specify the target and compare Re/Pr, buoyancy, development and solid-response distortions; identify what cannot be matched simultaneously.

original_question: How do distributed volumetric heating versus externally applied heating, different coolant properties and nonuniform losses affect applicability? Do not imply neutronics, chemistry or other excluded physics are modeled.
review_answer: Equal total power does not establish equivalent thermal forcing. Volumetric fluid heating, wall heaters and solid heating change gradients, solid storage, buoyant-head distribution and source-to-fluid delay. Nonuniform losses and cooling similarly alter the circulation-driving temperature field. Preserve source partition and conjugate paths in the reduction, and compare source arrangements only under declared common boundaries. Use measured or modeled actual heat delivery rather than assuming a command equals deposited power.
research_followup: Use the supported motivation and source/solid/fluid distinctions in the proposal; quantitative transfer is a later named-circuit assessment.
topic: Source, property and loss differences
integrated_takeaway: Equal total power does not establish equivalent thermal forcing.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Declare electrical-wall versus volumetric heating, composition/property range and nonuniform losses; keep omitted reactor physics outside the representation claim.

original_question: Verify the raw-note claim of an approximately “25% MSRE heat-balance discrepancy”: what was compared, which denominator/time period, and what primary report supports it? If unverified or wrong, say so and do not repeat it as motivation. Separately determine whether critical heat flux is relevant to our intended single-phase scope or belongs to a different problem.
review_answer: The acquired Gabbard original does not substantiate a generic approximately 25% MSRE heat-balance discrepancy with a verified denominator and time period. Exclude that number. The defensible historical lesson concerns property revisions, installed power metrology, exchanger/radiator performance and distinct discrepancies. Boiling critical heat flux is not the default limitation of the present single-phase sensible-heat scope. Allowable material/sensor temperatures, heat flux and sensible liquidus margin should be named instead.
research_followup: Do not restore the excluded quantitative claim; no further research is required for its exclusion in this review.

Predict primary/wall temperatures, circulation and cooler duty rather than supplying the same targets as boundaries. For transitions add allowed initial-state information, forcing history or scenarios, horizon and hidden-state uncertainty. original_question: Which QoIs require field reconstruction rather than bulk temperatures? How should bulk, mixing-cup, area-average, centerline, point, wall and sensor-filtered temperatures be related? Can reduction preserve duty while losing local extrema?
review_answer: Point, centerline, wall and sensor-filtered temperatures need distinct operators. Area mean is not mixing-cup enthalpy temperature; variable cp requires enthalpy integration. A model can preserve total duty while redistributing temperature incorrectly and losing extrema. Use CFD to define state-to-sensor/profile maps and test those separately from integrated budgets. With countertransport or nearly zero net flow, retain separate signed enthalpy streams rather than normalize by a nearly cancelling mass flux.

original_question: How can a model estimate unobserved hot/cold spots with honest uncertainty when experiments sample only a few locations? What supports a location claim versus a conservative bound?
review_answer: Sparse observations alone do not determine arbitrary unobserved hot/cold spots. Use an explicit spatial/closure family, jointly admissible parameter and boundary uncertainty, and a qualified CFD/reconstruction reference; propagate that support into extrema. Without those restrictions, report measured-location margins or conditional bounds, not a unique unmeasured location. A bound is conditional on the retained model/discrepancy class and domain, and a posterior credible interval is not automatically an externally validated coverage guarantee.

original_question: How do interpolation, observation operators, wall conduction and sensor dynamics alter comparisons with experiments? What data would distinguish sensor placement/calibration from missing physical transport?
review_answer: Apply interpolation, sensor footprint, contact conduction and response/timing in the forward observation operator before comparing predictions. Shared calibration correction does not remove centerline-to-bulk or outside-wall-to-contact mismatch. Compare model alternatives under the same calibration/placement uncertainty; independent reference/calibration records and contrasts with different physical sensitivity help distinguish causes. If boundary, sensor and closure effects remain observationally equivalent, report that confounding rather than naming a fitted bias a proven sensor correction.

original_question: Which tolerances should be set from operating decisions versus statistical/measurement resolution? Identify evidence needed before specifying numerical acceptance thresholds; do not choose arbitrary values for us.
review_answer: Set operating usefulness from a declared decision or margin, measurement distinguishability from its joint uncertainty, and numerical adequacy from target-specific solver error. They are separate requirements. This review uses symbolic target tolerances and specifies error, interval-width and margin rules without inventing values. The already specified study outputs suffice to finish the literature deliverables; assigning numerical thresholds later does not require reopening their purpose or asking for another adviser interview now.

original_question: Compare lumped RC/thermal networks, segmented conjugate fluid-wall-insulation networks, reduced regional grey-box models, 1D natural-circulation models and quasi-1D/low-order spatial models. State equations, physical meanings and reduction assumptions.
review_answer: A lumped RC model aggregates thermal storage/exchange; a segmented conjugate model retains fluid/wall/insulation and directional enthalpy; a regional grey-box model identifies effective storage/couplings; a 1D circulation model adds buoyancy/resistance and possibly inertia; a low-order spatial model retains profile/mode information. M1/M2/M3 are specifically the audited steady no-flow, prescribed-flow and scalar-flow-root hierarchy. Their state meanings and prediction roles differ. Compare a conventional physical model, the proposed framework and a modest predictor rather than implementing every family.
research_followup: Instantiate the recommended small physical hierarchy and test the selected closure/reduction assumptions.

integrated_takeaway: A lumped RC model aggregates thermal storage/exchange; a segmented conjugate model retains fluid/wall/insulation and directional enthalpy; a regional grey-box model identifies effective storage/couplings; a 1D circulation model adds buoyancy/resistance and possibly inertia; a low-order spatial model retains profile/mode information.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Compare lumped/regional, segmented conjugate, circulating 1D and low-order spatial models by their actual states/equations and information requirements.

original_question: Which physical states and heat paths are necessary to preserve thermal storage, losses, duty, buoyancy and local temperature gradients? How are axial wall conduction, insulation/contact, radiation, supports and source deposition treated?
review_answer: Retain paths that carry source, rejection, ambient loss, storage or transport relevant to the target. Wall/insulation/contact and axial conduction must have explicit inclusion or bounded-elimination assumptions. Radiation uses kelvin and an appropriate surface/view-factor model. State enrichment must improve a declared prediction or expose a limit; fitting many internal coefficients does not make them physical properties. Storage-only capacity cannot change an exact steady solution, although cp still enters steady enthalpy advection.
research_followup: Instantiate the recommended small physical hierarchy and test the selected closure/reduction assumptions.

original_question: When do steady momentum closure, transient inertia and advection need separate treatment? Explain circulation branch/reversal, low-flow limits and stability concerns where relevant; do not conflate passive temperature relaxation with full coupled hydrodynamics.
review_answer: An algebraic steady momentum root supplies a circulation branch, not a transient stability result. Transient inertia and directional enthalpy transport are separate mechanisms; a passive temperature relaxation alone does not describe coupled hydrodynamics. Treat zero flow and sign changes consistently, search/report possible branches and retain a dynamical model to claim reversal or stability. Use classical loop models as verification only with their own heating, mixing, resistance and inertia assumptions.

original_question: How should natural/mixed/forced convection, entrance/development effects, curved connections, conjugate heat transfer and property variation inform closure choices? Distinguish established correlation limits from proposed corrections.
review_answer: Choose closures using hydraulic/thermal development, source and wall conditions, orientation, property variation, buoyancy and geometry. Treat fully developed values as justified limits, and ideal entrance formulas as source-bounded candidates. Bends and source changes motivate descriptors; they do not prove a universal complete reset. Section/cluster losses need pressure-plane and recovery conventions. The final review recommends development-first qualification and closure-use records; it does not transfer every TAMU coefficient or mixed-convection threshold to ACU/VCU.

original_question: Compare fixed material/correlation models, a small fitted grouped-parameter network, conventional projection ROMs, operator inference, learned closure hybrids, Gaussian-process surrogates and other credible data-driven baselines. Include a simple model that can defeat an overcomplicated proposed method.
review_answer: Use a small fixed-correlation physical model with ordinary covariance-aware parameter learning as the serious baseline; compare the reduction/closure framework under matched information and a modest regularized response surface or GP. Add one spatial reconstruction alternative when the target requires it. Projection and learned-operator models require declared state/snapshot access and constraint handling; sparse probe data do not automatically supply it. Preserve a simple model that can win. Model-selection and inference comparisons are distinct experiments.

original_question: For each family, explain accessible data requirements, cost, interpretability, conservation/positivity/stability, uncertainty, extrapolation and falsifiable failure modes. Recommend a minimal comparison set rather than requiring every family to be implemented.
review_answer: Physical networks need geometry/properties and a limited parameter set; they are interpretable but can be nonidentifiable. Projection needs state/residual access; learned operators need informative trajectories and structural assumptions; direct emulators need representative input-output cases. None guarantees extrapolation, stability, conservation or uncertainty coverage by its name. Score the same target and online information, account for development and online cost separately, and admit complexity only when it resolves a demonstrated limitation.

original_question: What does the reduction actually do: aggregate control volumes, lump resistances/capacities, project fields, infer operators, learn spatial reconstruction, or close unresolved transport? Distinguish those contributions.
review_answer: Declare separately the aggregation from fields to conserved quantities, elimination/lumping of states, projection onto a basis/manifold, closure of unresolved transport and reconstruction to observations/fields. Learning an HTC or effective resistance is closure identification; it is not automatically projection or state reduction. Every operation needs an equation and information contract. Compare its error contribution using budgets and target outputs, and avoid claiming that a new set of software modules alone defines a new reduction method.
research_followup: Specify and assess the selected reduction/closure and observation operators using the CFD development contract.

original_question: Can CFD support observable-consistent bulk-to-local temperature and wall-flux maps, or development-conditioned heat-transfer closures that improve predictions beyond fixed averages? What information would those maps require at online inference time?
review_answer: Yes: paired interface heat rates, signed enthalpy fluxes and cross-sectional temperature/velocity information can support development-conditioned transfer closures and sensor/profile maps. Export the fields and averaging conventions in A§14. Test whether the descriptors used in development can be inferred from reduced states and operational inputs. If future CFD fields are still supplied online, label the result conditional. Withhold cases and separate closure, reconstruction and end-to-end predictive errors. This specification can be defined now with the computational team.

original_question: How do goal-oriented/adjoint, balanced, POD/Galerkin, nonlinear/manifold, structure-preserving and data-driven methods select states to retain? Which are feasible with sparse experiment data and delayed CFD?
review_answer: Aggregation gives interpretable compartments; POD prioritizes snapshot reconstruction in a chosen norm; balanced methods incorporate input-output behavior; goal-oriented methods target a functional; nonlinear manifolds address nonlinear state representation; constrained methods preserve declared structure. They differ in state/residual/adjoint and training-data needs. Select physical reduction with optional temperature reconstruction now; use a projection/manifold branch only for a demonstrated limitation with the required CFD access. No full proof or production reproduction of every family is claimed.

original_question: Compare closure correction, state enrichment and explicit extra physics. What diagnostics decide that a closure is inadequate rather than merely poorly calibrated? How do we prevent a fitted coefficient absorbing wrong geometry or boundary conditions?
review_answer: First verify geometry, source/sink accounting and observation operators, then compare closure correction and state enrichment under the same data and nuisance flexibility. Structured residuals across conditions, failed budget closure, unsupported inferred coefficients or incompatible reconstructed profiles can reject an assumption; one poor fit cannot uniquely name a missing mechanism. A richer model that absorbs wrong boundaries is not a demonstrated physical improvement. Withhold conditions and test a controlled change to the reduction/closure rule.

original_question: Which methods preserve energy, dissipation, positive capacities and appropriate transport direction? Are passivity/port-Hamiltonian or related frameworks suitable for dissipative thermal-advection networks, and which assumptions prevent direct transfer from mechanical/Hamiltonian examples?
review_answer: Use shared face enthalpy fluxes and paired internal exchanges, positive capacities, admissible conductances and consistent signed flow. Conservation, uniform-temperature equilibrium, positive temperature and passivity are different checks. Port-Hamiltonian approaches are relevant only after deriving suitable storage/ports for the actual thermal-advection system. A mechanical energy norm or a stable learned matrix does not establish thermodynamic validity. Conservative projection is prior art, and feasibility must be checked if adopted.
evidence: PF04 directed-network audit; S79/S80 scoped; A§2/13/16/17

proposed_work_or_expansion: Check paired internal transfers, uniform equilibrium, positive capacities/temperature and signed transport separately; derive suitable ports/storage before invoking passivity.

original_question: How should we split cases for closure training, method selection and final unseen assessment to avoid leaking CFD snapshots or experimental targets? Compare leave-regime/geometry/case-out assessment with random time-point splits.
review_answer: Hold out whole cases, regimes or geometries according to the intended generalization claim. Random points from one run/CFD field assess interpolation and leak common history/physics into the split. Use distinct development, selection and final-assessment roles; freezing only parameter fitting is insufficient if the same cases selected mesh, observation maps or closure families. Reclassify exposed or anchor cases honestly and reserve subsequent evidence. The plan can be specified without processing any held operating dataset.
research_followup: Specify and assess the selected reduction/closure and observation operators using the CFD development contract.

proposed_work_or_expansion: Split by physical run/case/condition and record exposure/refitting history; do not use random time-point splits as evidence of independent physical generalization.

original_question: Define useful descriptors of extent: reverse-flow volume/area fraction, separation/reattachment length, recirculating region size, signed local axial flow or exchange/transport measures. Which are robust in 3D, sensitive to averaging/frame/threshold, or ambiguous in buoyant curved flow? Distinguish persistent structures from temporal intermittency.
review_answer: Use section-normal signed velocity to define reverse area/transport fractions, and a declared region/connectivity convention for cell extent, separation/reattachment or exchange. Local backflow is not itself a closed cell or loop reversal. State threshold, coordinate/frame, averaging and persistence; the reversed mask of a mean field differs from mean reversed occupancy. Report dimensional transport near vanishing net flow. These are analysis definitions to test on CFD, not universal onset thresholds or measured TRIDENT extent.

original_question: How can the heat-transfer effect be quantified: changes in wall heat flux, local/region-integrated transfer, fluid/wall extrema, effective transport or temperature asymmetry? HTC definitions may become ill-conditioned when the driving temperature difference is small or changes sign; examine alternatives.
review_answer: Prefer regional/interface heat rates, enthalpy redistribution, thermal asymmetry and fluid/wall extrema with a common boundary contract. An HTC additionally needs a well-conditioned, explicitly defined wall-to-fluid temperature difference and averaging area. If that difference crosses zero, report dimensional flux or a richer representation instead of an enormous apparent coefficient. A correlation-evaluated Nu is not an independently measured heat-transfer effect. Match spatial/time windows between flow and thermal descriptors.

original_question: What are valid counterfactual or controlled comparisons for attributing a heat-transfer change to recirculation rather than changed flow rate, geometry, boundary condition or thermal development? Correlation of two CFD outputs is not by itself attribution.
review_answer: Match source/sink histories, geometry, property range, net circulation or its declared control, and development information where feasible; change one representation/mechanism in a controlled model contrast. A CFD intervention that suppresses buoyancy or constrains velocity may change multiple pathways, so its causal interpretation must state those changes. Use observational results for association and predictive usefulness unless an isolating comparison exists. A robust closure benefit is useful even when a universal causal effect of recirculation is not identified.

original_question: Compare an effective closure, a two-zone exchange model, a local spatial correction and a richer velocity/temperature reconstruction. What is the simplest representation that can predict extent and thermal effect sufficiently for a declared QoI?

Add a throughflow-plus-cell or two-zone exchange state only when coherent compartments and their exchange can be supported. A full velocity-temperature reconstruction is later. Persistent cross-sectional countertransport may defeat one bulk state, while localized fitting recirculation can sometimes be represented by a qualified section closure. Choose by target error and evidence, not the appearance of a vortex contour.

Demonstrate ambiguity through constrained alternatives or target-support analysis; do not infer unique extent from a good fit. Thermal consequences may remain predictable even when flow topology is unsupported. Experimental agreement can assess the thermal observation map while extent remains CFD-defined and reference-conditional.

original_question: When Ethan's TAMU thesis arrives, what exact evidence should be extracted, and which applicability checks must precede use in Trident? Give a no-CFD/minimal-CFD/adequate-CFD feasibility ladder and a stopping criterion for claims that cannot be supported.
review_answer: The acquired Ethan thesis dossier already identifies geometry/fluid/BCs, sensor operators, mesh/time/QoI verification, validation separation, property/energy conventions and limitations to extract. Preserve its supplied version and original locators; discrepancy reconciliation remains outside this review. No spatial reference permits thermal observation claims; a few qualified cases permit conditional maps; an adequate held-out campaign permits bounded descriptor/reconstruction assessment. Stop extent or universal transfer claims when the required reference/identifiability is absent, without stopping the framework study.
research_followup: Generate the defined descriptors/reference contrasts and assess thermal consequences separately from experimental extent validation.

integrated_takeaway: The acquired Ethan thesis dossier already identifies geometry/fluid/BCs, sensor operators, mesh/time/QoI verification, validation separation, property/energy conventions and limitations to extract.

original_question: What are the structurally and practically identifiable parameter combinations for steady and passive/transient thermal networks with sparse temperature observations? Compare sensitivity rank, Fisher information, profile likelihood, posterior geometry and synthetic recovery.
review_answer: Use exact invariance/structural analysis for a specified model, local sensitivity/Fisher information for local practical support, nuisance-reoptimized profile likelihood for nonelliptic ambiguity, posterior geometry for prior-conditioned uncertainty and synthetic recovery for implementation/information checks. These tools answer different questions. Narrow Hessian intervals or full local rank do not prove global physical identification. Report supported combinations and target ranges. CSEM/CAL and thermal-network literature already contain rank/compensation results; repeat diagnostics are groundwork.
research_followup: Apply covariance-aware supported-parameter learning and nuisance/target profiling to the selected physical model.
topic: Supported parameters versus a good fit
integrated_takeaway: Use exact invariance/structural analysis for a specified model, local sensitivity/Fisher information for local practical support, nuisance-reoptimized profile likelihood for nonelliptic ambiguity, posterior geometry for prior-conditioned uncertainty and synthetic recovery for implementation/information checks.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Use invariance, sensitivity/Fisher rank, nuisance-reoptimized profiles, posterior geometry and synthetic recovery for their distinct purposes; report target/combination support.

original_question: Derive the common G–C scale ambiguity, the conditions under which measured steady net power or fixed inventories break it, and the remaining ambiguities in multiregion networks. When is sequential steady-G then transient-C defensible versus a joint fit?
review_answer: For passive C dT/dt = −G(T−Ta), common positive scaling of C and G leaves the trajectory unchanged; only G/C is fixed. Known net steady power at nonzero temperature rise supplies G, then C=Gτ; trusted inventory capacity is another anchor. Residual duty, observation bias or changing exchange invalidate a naive sequence. A distributed network retains internal ambiguities after one scale anchor. Carry anchor uncertainty and compare joint fitting when steady and transient stages share uncertain parameters.
evidence: A§6 EQ05/§17; S70/S77; PF04 analysis; completed CAL-003
research_followup: Apply covariance-aware supported-parameter learning and nuisance/target profiling to the selected physical model.
topic: Absolute energy scale and sequential learning
integrated_takeaway: For passive C dT/dt = −G(T−Ta), common positive scaling of C and G leaves the trajectory unchanged; only G/C is fixed.
proposed_work_or_expansion: State which measured-duty or inventory datum anchors scale; propagate that uncertainty and compare sequential steady/dynamic learning with joint inference when they share uncertain quantities.

original_question: How do uncertain initial insulation/structure temperatures, hidden fluid-wall splits, parameter variation and unknown residual heater/cooler duty confound capacity estimates? Compare approaches for treating those nuisance quantities.
review_answer: Initial wall/insulation states, hidden fluid-solid splits, residual heater/cooler duty and changing heat paths can mimic a capacity or time constant. Use measured support where available, jointly estimated hidden states or bounded scenarios with shared parameters across cases. Do not grant the richer model arbitrary target-informed initial states. Compare joint inference with sequential learning and propagate earlier-stage uncertainty; report failure to distinguish capacity from boundary/initial-state effects rather than assigning every lag to material storage.
research_followup: Apply covariance-aware supported-parameter learning and nuisance/target profiling to the selected physical model.
topic: Hidden initial states and residual duty
integrated_takeaway: Initial wall/insulation states, hidden fluid-solid splits, residual heater/cooler duty and changing heat paths can mimic a capacity or time constant.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Use common initial-state information and bounded hidden-solid participation; do not grant a richer model target-informed starts or identify every observed lag as material capacity.

original_question: Compare deterministic constrained fits, regularization, Bayesian/hierarchical identification and model-discrepancy approaches. Which parameters can remain physical, and when does an effective correction lose that interpretation?
review_answer: Begin with a constrained covariance-aware physical fit and profiles. Add Bayesian/hierarchical inference when shared parameters, uncertainty propagation and defensible priors warrant it; regularization stabilizes estimation but must be declared as information. Use discrepancy only with a specified physical/output role and assessment. A coefficient remains physically interpretable only to the degree that model structure, boundary/observation assumptions and independent support justify that interpretation. Report effective groups when several physical mechanisms are inseparable.
research_followup: Apply covariance-aware supported-parameter learning and nuisance/target profiling to the selected physical model.
topic: Constrained fits, priors and effective parameters
integrated_takeaway: Begin with a constrained covariance-aware physical fit and profiles.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Compare deterministic/regularized and probabilistic alternatives where needed; report when a fitted group is predictive but cannot retain a unique physical interpretation.

original_question: How can boundary error, parameter error, observation error and structural discrepancy be distinguished? What priors/independent experiments are required, and how can a flexible discrepancy model conceal missing physics?
review_answer: Boundary, parameter, sensor and structural errors can produce the same residuals. Independent calibration/boundary information, multiple conditions with different sensitivities and competing physical error models can help discriminate them; one temperature fit cannot. A flexible output discrepancy may improve fit while hiding incorrect physics, especially for unobserved targets. Embed a constrained closure correction when physical propagation is needed, preserve conservation, and report joint ambiguity if evidence cannot separate explanations.
research_followup: Apply covariance-aware supported-parameter learning and nuisance/target profiling to the selected physical model.

integrated_takeaway: Boundary, parameter, sensor and structural errors can produce the same residuals.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Use independent anchors and residual/case contrasts to test competing explanations; a flexible discrepancy must not conceal omitted heat paths or unsupported target sensitivity.

original_question: How should experiment and CFD be fused without counting the same calibration information twice or treating CFD as exact truth? Compare multi-fidelity, modular/cut approaches and explicit cross-facility discrepancy where appropriate.
review_answer: Use separate CFD and experimental observation/error operators with shared physical parameters only where appropriate. Track common measured boundaries, calibration and property inputs so conditioned CFD is not counted as an independent repeat. A modular closure-map-then-experiment workflow can make the information flow transparent; fully joint inference is an alternative if feedback matters. Multifidelity discrepancy must distinguish simulator differences from physical discrepancy. The proposed workflow is not claimed equivalent to joint Bayes or automatically identifying every closure.
research_followup: Apply covariance-aware supported-parameter learning and nuisance/target profiling to the selected physical model.

original_question: Build a source/dependence taxonomy covering random and systematic measurement effects, calibration, drift, correlated channels/time, geometry, material properties, boundaries/power, initial states, parameters, numerics, CFD and reduction/model discrepancy. Distinguish a lack of knowledge from a justified probability distribution.
review_answer: Start from primitive sources: shared calibration references/coefficient errors; channel noise, installation/drift/time; geometry/material/property laws; deposited power and secondary/ambient boundaries; hidden initial states; learned parameters/closure families; numerical error and CFD/reference inadequacy; and transfer distortion. Represent dependence explicitly and separate stochastic variability from bounded lack of knowledge. The existing VCU calibration set is one component with applicability/coverage limits, not proof of a total uncertainty budget. The source taxonomy and proposed representation are in A§8/15.
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.

integrated_takeaway: Start from primitive sources: shared calibration references/coefficient errors; channel noise, installation/drift/time; geometry/material/property laws; deposited power and secondary/ambient boundaries; hidden initial states; learned parameters/closure families; numerical error and CFD/reference inadequacy; and transfer distortion.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Populate calibration/channel/time, geometry/property/input, initial-state, parameter, numerical/reference and discrepancy components; leave unknowns explicit rather than assigning zero variance.

original_question: Compare local linear propagation, Monte Carlo/quasi-Monte Carlo, polynomial-chaos/collocation, ensembles, posterior predictive propagation and surrogate-assisted methods. Identify assumptions, computational budgets and failure near strong nonlinearities or regime changes.
review_answer: Use linear covariance propagation for locally smooth, well-conditioned mappings and joint Monte Carlo for the primary nonlinear parameter/boundary/discrepancy propagation. Quasi-Monte Carlo, polynomial chaos/collocation and surrogate-assisted sampling are optional accelerators when dimension, smoothness and evaluation cost justify them; their convergence must be checked on the target. Near reversal, switching, singular ratios or extrema/event changes, local Gaussian assumptions can fail. Numerical sampling convergence and predictive validity are separate tests.
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.
topic: Propagation method and nonlinear failure limits
integrated_takeaway: Use linear covariance propagation for locally smooth, well-conditioned mappings and joint Monte Carlo for the primary nonlinear parameter/boundary/discrepancy propagation.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Compare local covariance and joint sampling on selected targets; justify any acceleration by dimension/smoothness/cost and check reversal/event/small-denominator behavior.

original_question: How should covariance from shared instruments, derived duties/flow estimates, common ambient forcing and jointly estimated parameters be retained? Distinguish conditional Type A mean uncertainty from full prediction accuracy.
review_answer: Compute secondary duty, loss allocation and inferred primary flow from one shared set of primitive draws/covariances. Do not score duty and its ingredient temperatures/flow as independent replicates. Repeated use of a property law or calibration reference requires the same shared realization. For Q/Δh retain covariance and instability near Δh=0; include omitted storage/heat-loss/point-to-bulk error in the measurement model. A small propagated band on a dependent derived estimate is not independent flow validation.
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.
topic: Shared instruments and derived outputs
integrated_takeaway: Compute secondary duty, loss allocation and inferred primary flow from one shared set of primitive draws/covariances.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Reuse the same uncertain primitive wherever it appears in duty, flow or margins; retain temporal/channel dependence and distinguish repeatability from installed prediction accuracy.

original_question: How can uncertain closures/operators be propagated through steady and transient ROMs while maintaining physical constraints? Compare Bayesian operator inference and neural/operator methods against simpler constrained networks with uncertain parameters.
review_answer: Parameterize or constrain positive capacities/conductances and paired exchanges; use energy-consistent signed fluxes and declared closure domains. Sampled closures/operators must retain those requirements or be flagged/rejected consistently. A stable mean operator does not ensure stable posterior draws. Mathematical stability certificates apply to stated model classes and need not preserve true physical branch behavior. Treat positivity, conservation, passivity, input-response validity and uncertainty calibration as distinct properties.
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.
topic: Physical constraints for uncertain operators
integrated_takeaway: Parameterize or constrain positive capacities/conductances and paired exchanges; use energy-consistent signed fluxes and declared closure domains.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Check admissibility for individual parameter/closure draws; a stable mean operator does not establish stability, conservation or physical branch behavior for every realization.

original_question: What does “calibrated uncertainty” mean in this setting? Compare coverage, interval width/sharpness, likelihood or proper scores and conditional/regime checks, with small independent sample sets. Avoid equating bootstrap bands, confidence intervals, credible intervals and scenario envelopes.
review_answer: Report prediction error/bias, residual structure, interval width and proper predictive scores on whole independent cases. Coverage needs an appropriate number and design of independent outcomes; a few runs do not establish rare-tail reliability. Distinguish parameter intervals, conditional credible intervals, scenario envelopes and empirically calibrated predictive coverage. Keep calibration/selection exposure visible; widening bands until all development data lie inside is not evidence of useful uncertainty. Use the same target and observation model for all competitors.
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.
topic: What uncertainty calibration would mean
integrated_takeaway: Report prediction error/bias, residual structure, interval width and proper predictive scores on whole independent cases.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Label scenario, confidence, credible and predictive intervals; assess bias, interval width and coverage/proper scores only at the independent-case scale the evidence supports.

original_question: How should uncertainty in time/location of extrema, threshold crossing, settling time and freeze margin be reported? What can be bounded if a full probabilistic model is unjustified?
review_answer: Propagate joint state/closure/input/reference uncertainty into the complete extremum or event functional, not separate independent point bands. Record the probability/support of no crossing, competing locations and multiple extrema when relevant. Nonunique extrema and grazing threshold crossings make linear approximations unreliable. Report location only at the spatial/time resolution supported by observations and CFD; otherwise provide a region or bound. Sparse sensor minima/maxima are sampled extrema, not the field extrema by definition.
evidence: S72/S75/S76 target operators; analyst specification; A§5/8/14; B§8

integrated_takeaway: Propagate joint state/closure/input/reference uncertainty into the complete extremum or event functional, not separate independent point bands.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Propagate joint uncertainty through the whole spatial/time functional; retain no-crossing possibilities, competing extrema and unsupported-location bounds.

original_question: How can we separate numerical/CFD error and model discrepancy, and avoid double-counting residuals? Which uncertainty sources dominate the decision and should guide experimental/CFD effort?
review_answer: Estimate numerical sensitivity/error for the actual target using spatial, temporal, modal and sampling/extraction checks. Boundary/property and physical-model uncertainty are separate. Mesh agreement chosen partly by experimental fit is selection evidence, and half a mesh spread is not a universal uncertainty estimate. Qualify recirculation masks and heat-flux extraction independently of loop mean temperature. Keep numerical and physical error contributions separate unless an explicitly joint model combines them. No normative ASME compliance is claimed.
evidence: S19 Table5; S20 Table3; S29 verification dossier; A§10/14
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.
topic: Numerical reference error versus model discrepancy
integrated_takeaway: Estimate numerical sensitivity/error for the actual target using spatial, temporal, modal and sampling/extraction checks.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Qualify target-specific solver/CFD uncertainty and avoid counting the same residual twice; prioritize new evidence by consequential sensitivity rather than convenience.

original_question: What exactly can real-time inverse/UQ methods such as NEMO estimate, under what linear/nonlinear parameterization and noise assumptions? Does that match our unknowns and data, or should it remain a later comparator? Differentiate acceleration of inference from a complete treatment of model-form uncertainty.
review_answer: NEMO exploits a problem structure separating nonlinear parameter dependence from linear inversion variables and a reduced inverse representation. It is a possible accelerator only if the ROM inverse problem actually admits that structure over its domain. General buoyancy/property/closure/hidden-state learning need not do so. Verify the forward/inverse factorization and approximation error before adoption; fast inverse evaluation is neither new information nor total model-form uncertainty. It is an optional comparator, not the default methodology.
research_followup: Populate and propagate the primitive joint uncertainty model; assess predictive uncertainty on appropriate independent cases.
topic: Real-time inverse acceleration and its limits
integrated_takeaway: NEMO exploits a problem structure separating nonlinear parameter dependence from linear inversion variables and a reduced inverse representation.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Check whether a NEMO-type nonlinear/linear factorization fits the actual inverse variables and hidden states; keep it an optional comparator, not total model-form UQ.

original_question: What is the smallest informative design for separating net heat loss, regional G, participating C, ambient effects and fluid/solid coupling? Compare steady duties at multiple temperatures, warm/cold relaxations, known-power holds/shutdowns and independent heater/cooler changes.
review_answer: Enumerate physically feasible choices from Nick phases rather than optimizing arbitrary new instruments or controls. Compare candidates on target uncertainty, nuisance-aware model discrimination and robustness/cost. Start with source/sink/property contrasts that make fixed and development-informed closures predict observably different outcomes. A parameter-information optimum is not automatically best for the engineering target or validation relevance. If rankings change materially under plausible boundary/observation errors, report that sensitivity before claiming an optimal test.
research_followup: Map the existing phase plan to information/anchor/selection/assessment roles and compare feasible contrasts.

proposed_work_or_expansion: Compare feasible steady anchors, warm/cold relaxation, known-input holds/shutdowns and independent source/sink variation against the selected target and competing explanations.

original_question: What must be measured to establish an absolute energy scale? Address secondary flow/temperature/property uncertainty, actual versus commanded input, electrical deposition/parasitics, residual duty and common sensor biases.
review_answer: Use either an independently supported deposited-duty/secondary-energy anchor at a steady condition or a justified inventory/capacity anchor, and propagate its uncertainty. Passive temperatures alone identify ratios; voltage/setpoint alone is not watts. Global heat balance does not identify regional allocation or every network coefficient. The existing phase sequence provides places to assign these roles; no bulk data or instrument reupload is required to define the analysis. A case used as an anchor becomes calibration for the affected claim.
research_followup: Map the existing phase plan to information/anchor/selection/assessment roles and compare feasible contrasts.

proposed_work_or_expansion: Name measured versus nominal electrical/secondary inputs, source partition, residual duty and common biases; preserve CAL-019 nominal assumptions without calling them metered fluid duty.

original_question: What is an evidence-based choice of input excitation, duration, rate, repeat count and sensor placement? Discuss bandwidth, time-scale separation, autocorrelation, thermal equilibrium versus stationary operation, and conditioning. Do not invent facility-safe setpoints or assume arbitrary protocols can be executed.
review_answer: Choose durations and sampling from the modes/settling/event targets and their observation/initial-state uncertainties, not a universal number of time constants. Resolve the fastest retained response without treating correlated samples as independent cases; preserve enough time to constrain slow storage. Prefer independent source/sink variations that separate candidate effects and use repeated conditions to assess path/repeatability. Extra sensors or repeats are optional negotiated refinements, not assumed requirements for finishing this review.
research_followup: Map the existing phase plan to information/anchor/selection/assessment roles and compare feasible contrasts.
topic: Excitation, duration and sensor placement
integrated_takeaway: Choose durations and sampling from the modes/settling/event targets and their observation/initial-state uncertainties, not a universal number of time constants.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Justify rates/windows/repeats using bandwidth, thermal time scales, autocorrelation and conditioning; a stationary measured trace is not proof of negligible hidden storage.

original_question: Compare parameter-information objectives with QoI uncertainty reduction and model-discrimination experimental design. Which is most useful when several model forms fit the same sparse data?
review_answer: Parameter design reduces supported parameter uncertainty; target design reduces uncertainty in a specified future quantity; discrimination separates competing model explanations; validation design selects evidence relevant to target-sensitive assumptions. Their optima can differ. Use a small finite feasible comparison first, include nuisance/input uncertainty and inspect scaling/estimator sensitivity. The existence of goal-oriented design is established prior work, so using it must support a specific reduction/closure question rather than serve as the novelty claim by itself.
research_followup: Map the existing phase plan to information/anchor/selection/assessment roles and compare feasible contrasts.
topic: Parameter information, target information and model discrimination
integrated_takeaway: Parameter design reduces supported parameter uncertainty; target design reduces uncertainty in a specified future quantity; discrimination separates competing model explanations; validation design selects evidence relevant to target-sensitive assumptions.
proposed_work_or_expansion: Compare actual feasible choices under nuisance/input uncertainty; report ranking sensitivity and computational cost rather than asserting a universal optimal experiment.

original_question: Which extra measurements offer the largest benefit, and which claims must be dropped if they cannot be obtained? Separate existing instruments, feasible metadata requests, additional instrument proposals and CFD-only evidence.
review_answer: Retain assessable sensor/regional/duty predictions when evidence cannot distinguish all internal mechanisms. Request targeted fields, boundary qualification or an independent anchor only when it changes a specific claim; otherwise report supported groups and conditional bounds. Lack of a local flow instrument restricts experimental extent validation, not all thermal reduction work. The collaborating CFD campaign can test field-level definitions and reconstruction while experiments test thermal observations. Unsupported whole-reactor or autonomous-control claims are dropped.
research_followup: Map the existing phase plan to information/anchor/selection/assessment roles and compare feasible contrasts.

proposed_work_or_expansion: Classify existing signals, feasible metadata, proposed instruments and CFD-only products; restrict only the unsupported claim when a desired measurement is unavailable.

Label every item proposed, not agreed. Identify case reallocation when an originally blind P3 case becomes a calibration anchor.

review_answer: Operational inputs are boundaries, commands converted through source models, properties and allowed initial information. CFD supplies internal fields, interface/section integrals and development/reference features during model development; experiments supply calibrated thermal/secondary observations and case metadata. Outputs include conservation budgets, sensor-consistent temperatures, duty, circulation and qualified reconstructed fields. Record imposed versus predicted quantities and common dependencies. The same output cannot silently serve as a measured boundary and independent prediction target in one score.

Compare the CFD observation operator with the real measurement rather than treating sparse thermal agreement as validation of the entire velocity field. Withhold conditions for reconstruction/descriptor transfer. Report field-reference error and physical-closure alternatives separately from ROM reduction error; numerical convergence alone does not establish experimental local-flow truth.

original_question: How do Reynolds/thermal development, transition assumptions, buoyancy treatment, gravity/pressure boundaries and conjugate walls affect applicability? Do not assume a turbulence model or a laminar regime from convenience.
review_answer: Record regime and convention-specific Re/Pr/buoyancy measures, source and wall boundary conditions, geometry/reset/recovery, variable properties and conjugate fluid-solid times. A correlation’s nominal laminar range does not establish development or absence of buoyancy distortion. Low-Pr, internally heated, water-channel or fixed-sink examples are conditional comparators. original_question: How can a limited CFD campaign discriminate candidate closures efficiently? What should be varied independently and held fixed? How should unavailable CFD change the minimum PhD demonstration rather than simply delay all work?
review_answer: Prioritize cases that distinguish the conventional and proposed closure/reconstruction rules under the same online information: nominal conditions, source/sink contrast, property/development contrast and a weak-flow limit. Export reusable section/interface/observation quantities from each case. Use QoI/adjoint or finite-difference sensitivity to target the contrast, but verify derivative/numerical error and nuisance robustness. More snapshots from the same case cannot replace independent condition contrasts; request richer fields only if the selected target needs them.

PC1 supplies steady what-if predictions; PC2 requires an initial-state/horizon/forcing contract; PC3 diagnoses wall response given later primary measurements. Useful steady comparisons can precede live transients. A future measured ambient input makes the forecast boundary-conditioned. None of these labels establishes automatic control or decision authority.

original_question: Which later startup/shutdown, pressure/level, trace-heating and freezing questions require new physics or data? Distinguish single-phase margin prediction from resolving solidification, blockage or multiphase processes. Separate advisory prototypes from actual control or unattended operation.
review_answer: Startup/shutdown forecasting needs appropriate source history, fluid/solid initial states, transport and possible inertia. Trace heating requires spatial delivery/control and losses. Pressure/level or gas/void behavior needs additional states/equations and evidence. A single-phase sensible-temperature margin above liquidus is distinct from latent heat, solidification fronts, blockage and multiphase processes. Keep advice/prototype output separate from control or unattended protection. Those extensions remain P2 unless explicitly selected and qualified.
evidence: S38/S51; original brief J4; A§2/11; B§4/9
research_followup: Integrate the qualified result contract collaboratively; test human-use/control claims separately if selected.

original_question: What are the closest prior methods—not only closest fluids/applications—for our proposed reduction/closure/identification/UQ framework? What do they already accomplish that we must not claim as new?
review_answer: The closest work includes thermal-network structure/identification and physical interpretation, goal-oriented reduction/calibration/design, embedded discrepancy, conjugate/stochastic loop dynamics, conservative/stable learned reduction and similarity. It also includes completed CSEM/CAL compensation, scale/rank and startup studies. These precedents defeat novelty claims based solely on physical equations, an extra wall state, parameter fitting, UQ bands or a target-aware objective. Compare specific procedures and results, not just papers using the same fluid.
research_followup: Test the framework against strongest conventional baselines and state the additional result actually established.

original_question: Identify 2–4 candidate contribution packages, each with a narrow claim, closest prior work, specific methodological difference, required data, fair baselines, testable hypotheses, failure criteria and realistic fallback. original_question: Could contributions arise from QoI-driven physical reduction, uncertainty-aware model/closure selection, observable-consistent spatial reconstruction, experiment–CFD identification, or assessment of achievable recirculation extent/thermal-effect prediction? What existing work most strongly challenges each idea?
review_answer: Potential advances are a reproducible development-informed reduction/closure rule, observation-consistent temperature reconstruction with a demonstrated domain, supported experiment–CFD parameter learning under shared uncertainty, or a qualified physical limit. Established methods strongly challenge each broad idea; new value must be precise and tested. For local extent, specify descriptor/reference and discriminate thermal consequences rather than promising full flow reconstruction. If a simpler representation suffices, the reduced adequate domain is itself a useful result when it exceeds existing findings.
research_followup: Test the framework against strongest conventional baselines and state the additional result actually established.

original_question: Distinguish method development, a reproducible procedure, new empirical physics, and a facility demonstration. Which combination would advance knowledge beyond a software integration/application exercise?
review_answer: Method development supplies a new or meaningfully improved rule and shows why/when it works. A reproducible procedure makes inference and assessment inspectable. New empirical physics provides independently qualified mechanism evidence. A facility demonstration shows performance at stated conditions. Software integration supports those results but is not interchangeable with them. The approved framework can combine these categories; the final thesis should state which additional result each work package establishes and avoid relabeling completed groundwork.
research_followup: Test the framework against strongest conventional baselines and state the additional result actually established.

integrated_takeaway: Method development supplies a new or meaningfully improved rule and shows why/when it works.
proposed_work_or_expansion: State which kind of contribution each work package would establish and what evidence separates it from implementation or a retrospective fit.

original_question: What could be a valuable negative result—for example, proving limits of sparse-data identification or showing when a richer spatial closure is unnecessary—and what evidence would make it publishable?
review_answer: A useful negative result states the model/evidence class, an ambiguity or adequacy boundary, a consequential engineering prediction and reproducible evidence beyond known scale/rank limitations or prior CSEM/CAL failures. Examples are two observation-consistent closures giving materially different targets, a descriptor that cannot be inferred online, or a simpler model matching the richer one over a qualified domain. A failed fit or absent CFD alone is insufficient. Independent cases or a precise analytical counterexample support the result.
research_followup: Test the framework against strongest conventional baselines and state the additional result actually established.
